text:
alex: FYI — seeing p99 latency spikes on a subset of us-west GPU hosts after the driver roll (12.2.1). Traces point to the kernel selector flipping to FlashAttn_v2 for short (<=64) sequences. Repro on 3 hosts. Anyone else?

maya: saw something similar in staging this morning. Batcher heuristic flipped because the seq-length histogram shifted slightly. KV prefetching started thrashing and evicting hot entries.

liam: can you paste the perf dump + kernel list? ping @infra-bot for the rollout details.

infra-bot: deploy: driver/12.2.1 rolled to us-west-2 (hosts: gpu-usw2-1, gpu-usw2-2, gpu-usw2-3, gpu-usw2-4) at 2026-07-04T02:17:34Z

alex: perf snapshot pasted below (trimmed):

```
kernel_profile:
  chosen_kernel: FlashAttn_v2
  heuristic_score: 0.82
  latency_p50: 10.2ms
  latency_p99: 245.7ms
  kv_cache_hits: 72%
  kv_cache_evictions_per_min: 48
fallback: FlashAttn_v1 p99 123.4ms
```

maya: looks like the selector's fingerprinting now prefers a VAOP fused path that is heavier on shared memory. For short batches that triggers extra shared-mem spilling and more ctx-switches -> KV eviction cycles.

noah: runtime supports env override: REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=flashattn:v1. Can we try that on one host?

alex: tried override on gpu-usw2-2. p99 went from ~248ms -> ~112ms. Throughput stayed stable. Rolling back the whole driver is heavier; prefer patching selector heuristics or pinning short-seq workloads to v1 until fixed.

liam: filing an incident now. I'll add perf traces and request infra-targeted rollback if canary fails. Actions: maya -> selector patch + tests, noah -> run a 10-host canary, alex -> collect more traces.

maya: working on a patch. Initial theory: selector score = alpha * est_flops - beta * scratch_mem. For short seq we should reduce the scratch_mem penalty (beta) — will push PR with new coeffs + perf runs.

alex: attaching one more trace snippet:

```
[trace-id: t-9f3c]
seq=32 batch=8 kernel=FlashAttn_v2 time_ms=230.4 kv_prefetches=12 evictions=9 ctx_switches=6
```

noah: starting canary on gpu-usw2-2,3,4 now. Will update in ~20m. :rocket: 

infra-bot: alert: noisy-tenant detected on gpu-usw2-3 (pid 4187 high-alloc). Confirmed co-located workload = s3-indexer spiking memory + allocations.

alex: interesting — noisy neighbor could be amplifying the selector decision. If memory pressure spikes, FlashAttn_v2's scratch mem cost becomes costlier and triggers more evictions. Let's also try evicting the noisy tenant during the canary.

noah: evicting non-critical workloads on gpu-usw2-3 now.

alex: update after eviction: p99 dropped from ~240ms -> ~130ms without any kernel override. So we have a clear interaction: driver selector change + noisy neighbor memory pressure.

liam: I will include that as a candidate root cause in the incident ticket: (1) driver fingerprinting changed kernel ranking; (2) co-located noisy tenant increased scratch pressure; (3) KV cache miss/eviction pattern amplified latency.

maya: continuing on the selector patch; also adding a short-seq unit test that simulates KV miss rate to prevent regressions.

alex: next steps: finish selector patch PR, run canary across 10 hosts, add eviction circuit-breaker to the scheduling agent for strong memory spikes. If canary fails we'll coordinate a targeted rollback of driver 12.2.1 in us-west-2.

noah: canary started — initial 10m looks good on gpu-usw2-2 & 4, p99 down ~50%. Will keep monitoring.

liam: thanks all. Good detective work. We'll keep this thread updated and I'll push the incident summary once we close. :thumbsup:
